items.title: Interview: Naoki Hamaguchi on the FFXIV FFVII Beyond the Lifestream Raid Series
items.summary: FFVII Remake trilogy director Naoki Hamaguchi talked about the FFXIV Beyond the Lifestream crossover raid series and its development.
items.content:
One of the big announcements coming out of the Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival events in 2026 involved a FFVII Remake raid series called Beyond the Lifestream for the FFXIV Evercold expansion . In addition to the MMORPG Director and Producer Naoki Yoshida and his team working on it, the FFVII remake trilogy team and Director Naoki Hamaguchi are involved in its development. Siliconera got a chance to check in with Hamaguchi to discuss development of the raid series, the upcoming crossover, and remake trilogy characters he’d like to see as possible Triple Triad cards.

Jenni Lada: When did work on the FFXIV FFVII Beyond the Lifestream raid series begin, and how many members of the Remake team have been assisting the MMORPG developers?

Naoki Hamaguchi: I believe it started about a year ago. When Yoshida-san and I were discussing launch timings for our respective titles, we had the idea of collaborating to generate excitement around the entire Final Fantasy franchise together, rather than launching each title one by one. That’s where it all began.

From there, the two teams worked out the details and the crossover content gradually took shape. I can’t share the specific numbers, but a tremendous number of staff members are contributing to the project when we include everyone working on the scenario, art, various assets, and lore supervision. The FFVII team isn’t merely supervising the project—this is more of a project where both teams are bringing their respective strengths together and creating something as one.

Exactly how involved are you in the process and what do you get to help assist on? Will you get to work on the narrative and make suggestions about bosses, or will you also be able to get more into Easter eggs and detailed apparel decisions as well? Naoki Hamaguchi: As the FFVII team, we’re contributing in a wide variety of areas: the scenario, characters, world-building, and art, as well as providing and supervising various assets. [Motomu] Toriyama-san and the FFXIV writing team have been the central figures in story planning, while Nojima-san is in charge of supervising the overall story, and [Tetsuya] Nomura-san oversees the character designs. We also have ongoing discussions with the FFXIV team regarding various aspects of development, including boss characters, visual presentation, and lore details.

Our role isn’t one where we merely supervise and point out which parts are right or wrong. In many instances, the FFXIV team shared their ideas and we put our heads together to figure out how they might work within the context of FFVII . As such, I think “co-production” better describes our team’s role, rather than “supervision.”

Have you been playing FFXIV as part of the preparation for this FFVII Beyond the Lifestream and, if so, what job and which raid series have you enjoyed most?

Naoki Hamaguchi: We’ve actually been paying attention to FFXIV and its community for quite some time, rather than researching them specifically for the crossover. I have a long-standing relationship with Yoshida-san and have followed FFXIV closely for many years.

This crossover has been a good opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of what kind of experience players are looking for in raid content, and how the FFXIV team fulfills those expectations. However, we did not offer suggestions on how the raid content itself should be created for this crossover. In that regard, we have a great deal of trust in the FFXIV team, who have been creating raids for many years. Rather, we focused on the setting, characters, and lore of FFVII and how those elements might harmonize with the raid experience that the FFXIV team was aiming to create.

In the past, elements of FFVII already appeared in FFXIV , with The Manderville Gold Saucer, the Diamond Weapon, Emerald Weapon, and Ruby Weapon boss fights, and the Fan Fest 2026 Hardy-Daytona mount and Red XIII and Yuffie minions. What did you learn from those additions when preparing for this raid series and how did feedback to those elements influence your creative process?

Naoki Hamaguchi: Elements from FFVII , such as the Gold Saucer and the Weapon boss fights, have been incorporated into FFXIV in various forms over the years. When we look at how players react to those game elements, we get the impression they’re not merely enjoying the visual references or names associated with FFVII ; they truly appreciate the setting, characters, and the essences that define FFVII .

This was also very important when we were brainstorming for this raid series. Our goal wasn’t simply to incorporate FFVII elements for the sake of it; rather, we wanted to deliver an experience that gives FFXIV players a taste of why FFVII has been loved for so many years. It’s thanks to all of the FFVII -related content that was already in the game, that we were able to take another step further with this crossover.

What’s interesting is that, whenever we try to do something with FFVII , both the creators and the fans naturally end up taking it very seriously (laughs). That may be one of the charms of the FFVII IP.

We’ve seen Final Fantasy XIV crossovers with other entries in the series like FFIV, FFXI, FFXIII, FFXV , and FFXVI before. How was your research and preparation for the FFXIV FFVII Beyond the Lifestream Raid influenced by these past encounters? Naoki Hamaguchi: Given that FFXIV had numerous wonderful crossovers in the past, we’re confident in the FFXIV team’s experience and expertise with crossovers.

on Google Preferred Source Google News Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap While Dawntrail's reception within the global Final Fantasy XIV community stands as relatively mixed, the white-hot buzz around Evercold and the beautiful yet ominous world of the Fourth is already helping the next expansion shape up to be one of the game's most highly-anticipated ones yet. Thanks to the series of graphic-related updates injected throughout Dawntrail's patch cycle, FF14 is now set to undergo a massive gameplay overhaul with Evercold's release, truly bringing the MMO into its next big era.

However, the hopes and dreams for Evercold don't just lie in those more technical updates. Two Fanfest keynotes worth of information have set the stage for what is increasingly looking like the game's most ambitious expansion to date, one that may finally even give the highly-acclaimed Shadowbringers expansion a run for its money after sitting alone at the top for so long.

Is there a reason behind these two characters getting singled out?

However, those keynotes have still left a number of hanging threads that players eagerly want answered, and normally we'd have to wait until the finale keynote in Tokyo to get any further inkling about where we're heading next in our adventure as the Warrior of Light. However, as it turns out, the final chunk of MSQ provided with the game's 7.56 patch update has given us not just a few hints of what to expect in the Fourth, but a full-on preliminary experience with a trove of lore about this frigid world straight from Visna herself.

The following article contains spoilers regarding characters and story anecdotes related to the Main Scenario Questline in the upcoming Evercold expansion in Final Fantasy XIV. Please read ahead with discretion.

After making her grand debut in the second version of the reveal trailer for Evercold at Fanfest, Visna's identity and purpose in the expansion was kept largely underwraps, with Yoshi-P simply telling us to hang tight until later in the year. However, that didn't stop the community at large from putting her few seconds on the big screen under a microscope . From the strange glowing tool she held up to the sky, to the falcon-type pet she interacted with, and a mysterious rune symbol that appeared in front of her during that interaction.

This all had players scrambling to put two and two together about the planned Physical Ranged DPS job for the expansion, with Bastion's big reveal as the Tank job now out of the way. Speculations immediately circled around something akin to a Ranger or Falconer, and composer Masayoshi Soken only fueled those rumors at a dev panel during the same Fanfest by playing sound effects that he claimed were from the new job. What stood out most prominently was the screech of what sounded very much like a bird creature.

That kept said speculations around a Falconer-esque job very much alive after Fanfest ended, though Visna's part in it all remained mysterious at best. There just wasn't enough to connect her to what were still just theories about this job. However, thanks to 7.56's final piece of the MSQ puzzle that connects Dawntrail to Evercold, it's pretty safe to say that Visna plays a pretty big part, not just in terms of the story but in giving context to what now very, very likely is the second job for the expansion.

During the MSQ's sequence of events, Visna and her crew show up aboard an airship to save your character and a couple of other Scions during an ambush by strange creatures, and she visibly brandishes a crossbow weapon. Then, on cue, she whistles and summons her Falcon familiar named Sigrnef to fight alongside her and fend off the creatures.

If this isn't a straight-up showcase of the Physical Ranged DPS, then there's no telling what else it could possibly be at this point. To boot, there's even a falcon-shaped insignia etched into the side of her crossbow weapon, which you can see above. Furthermore, there are other falcon embellishments on her outfit, such as the armband that's seen in this and other shots of the various cutscenes with her.

Meanwhile, the strange glowing wand we've seen her wield in the trailer is, in fact, a red herring as far as being job-related. The MSQ cutscenes reveal that this is a Reading Rod, a magical tool that's used to disclose the so-called "Brand" of an individual on the Fourth. Upon using it, Visna realizes that your Warrior of Light and accompanying Scions don't have Brands and initially panics in confusion. Further dialogue reveals the purpose of these Reading Rods and Brands, and it's equal parts fascinating and terrifying.

Your conversation with Visna after the dust settles goes into a staggering amount of entirely new lore about life on the Fourth, and how it came to be the way it is now. As previously revealed in the Fanfest trailers, the entire planet that makes up the Fourth is encased in ice, rendering anything and everything on the ground uninhabitable. To survive, those who still lived took to the skies above on massive floating airships, and that's how life on the Fourth remains to this day.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14's next expansion just teased a major Heavensward connection
items.summary: A familiar face may return in Evercold
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Willa Rowe Published Sep 10, 2026, 11:19 AM EDT News A familiar face may return in Evercold

Image: Square Enix Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Square Enix released patch 7.56 this week for Final Fantasy 14 , marking the last update the MMO will receive before the release of the Evercold expansion in January. With all of Dawntrail ' s loose threads already wrapped up, patch 7.56 paves the way for the game's next chapter. That was all to be expected, but what fans didn't expect was to see a character that had been dead for years.

Early in patch 7.56, which is called Trail to the Heavens, the Warrior of Light must teleport to the Fourth, a parallel world. The new ice-covered environment will serve as the main setting for Evercold , and this is the first time players have gone there. But during the teleportation process, there are flashes on the screen briefly showing a figure that looks exactly like Ysayle Dangoulain . That's a shock considering she tragically died near the end of the 2015 Heavensward expansion. At first, this was thought to be a flashback, but closer inspection reveals that Ysayle is wearing an entirely new outfit. That means this is a new asset in the game, signaling she may have a large part to play in Evercold . But is it even really Ysayle? That's the question fans are asking.

Image: Square Enix There is good news and bad news for those hoping this signals Ysayle's return. The bad news is that the community is in agreement that this is probably not the actual Ysayle who died in Heavensward . Even the Warrior of Light said they "had a vision of a woman who looked like Ysayle." The key distinction is that it is not actually her. The good news is that she still might be connected. Final Fantasy 14 has established in its lore that the world has been shattered into various shards; these are parallel worlds like the Fourth. The souls of individuals were also split across those shards. For example, Ardbert in Shadowbringers and the Warrior of Light are shards of the same soul. Whoever the mysterious woman is on the Fourth, she is likely a shard of Ysayle.

This would further strengthen the comparisons between Evercold and Heavensward . It doesn't seem to be a coincidence that the Warrior of Light's companions during Trail to the Heavens are Alphinaud and Estinien, two major characters from Heavensward who both interacted with Ysayle. This also opens up the possibility that other characters will return in similar ways, though I don't think the community could really take seeing a version of Haurchefant alive and well.

Image: Square Enix via Polygon Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Jump links Jump Links How to unlock Beastmaster in FFXIV Beastmaster Bestiary in FFXIV Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Final Fantasy 14 's second limited job, Beastmaster , has finally arrived with patch 7.56, so now you can collect a plethora of monsters to fight for you. Just like Blue Mage, this limited job is mostly for solo content and can't be used for regular quests and dungeons. Another similarity to Blue Mage: you won't be able to really fight until you run around Eorzea collecting logs for your bestiary .

After being teased by Beastmasters Pagaga and Lyon all the way back in Shadowbringers , players had an inkling that Beastmaster would make its appearance in the game eventually, but now you can finally play as one. Beastmaster also has its own version of Blue Mage's Masked Carnival challenge, called the Crucible of the Unbroken , where you'll need to use a range of collected skills to clear challenges.

Below we detail how to unlock Beastmaster in FFXIV , as well as list out where to find the beasts for your bestiary .

Update (Sept. 9) : We've added the remaining monsters to our list, so it's complete now. Happy hunting!

To unlock Beastmaster, you need to meet the following requirements:

If you check all those bosses, you can unlock Beastmaster by talking to the Excited Adventurer NPC (11.8, 13.6) in New Gridania , to start the quest "Strangers in the Wood."

Graphic: Julia Lee/Polygon | Source images: Square Enix via Polygon Beastmasters use striking gear (the same gear that Monks and Samurai use).

To catch these beasts, you'll need use "Capture" and then kill the monster. If you successfully catch it, it'll get logged in your bestiary. From there, you can assign it to the various horns to summon them to fight with you in battle.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV: Complete Edition for Nintendo Switch 2 Review
items.summary: FINAL FANTASY XIV Online Complete Edition is perfect for new players as it includes the base game and all expansions through Dawntrail.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV released on the Switch 2 as of a few weeks ago (depending on date of publication). I bought the Complete Edition , which gives access through Dawntrail … without knowing about the impending free trial version due out on August 4th. Still, I got 2 months+ worth of playtime to work with before having to get a Switch 2-specific subscription. So, how does it fare so far just after the A Realm Reborn expansion? Let’s find out!

Now, if you’re a Switch 2 newbie (like I am), then a lot of what is mentioned here will appear overwhelming to you, especially the plot of A Realm Reborn . Though, don’t worry, you do not need to play FFXIV 1.0 to understand FFXIV: A Realm Reborn ’s story, though having prior knowledge will help in understanding the context of certain flashbacks.You see, those masked individuals working with the Ixal (if your hometown is New Gridinia, more on that later) and in mysterious flashback cutscenes detailing the Primal Bahamut Dalahmud Moon that brought about the end of 1.0 are Ascions, aka: Paragons.

Their ability to summon creatures and possess people comes into play throughout A Realm Reborn and later expansions, and if you stick with it through all this story (there’s so much and constantly more coming into 2027 and beyond with Evercold ), you’ll discover the conflict between the Ascions and the Scions of the Seventh Dawn, with so many implications and events following these that I DARE not spoil. Yda and Papalymo are the first two story-significant characters you’ll meet, as a heads-up.

One of the downsides of Final Fantasy XIV: Complete Edition on Switch 2 is the need to pay a separate subscription fee entirely separate from the NOT-REQUIRED Switch Online. Yeah, in addition to needing any version of the game to play, nearly 150 GBs on space on your internal storage or MicroSD Express card, you also need a SEPARATE subscription to play the game past the free month grace period on Switch 2!! Yes, it’s annoying. Does it take away from the fun I am having right now? Hmm… a little. Thankfully, paying that fee is a bit easier than I thought. Just use the Nintendo eShop.

The game shines with its Xenoblade Chronicles -esque approach to combat. Each attack is on a cooldown after use. The more beneficial an attack or buff is, the longer it takes to recharge. Which attack you follow up with in combat after the previous one can offer benefits like increased damage to an enemy, for example, with the Lancer\Dragoon’s True Thrust following the use of a vorpal blade.

On the performance side of the gameplay, when dealing with less than 8 NPCs in one area at a time, like in a city or overworld, the FPS is generally 60, for BOTH docked and handheld (I don’t care about FPS as long as it’s stable and PLAYABLE). In the city or certain intense areas, the FPS is at a steady 30.

The music as always is excellent. the theme that capped off 1.0, known as “Answers”, is the most beautiful and best song in the entire franchise. Playing mainly in the raid dungeon known as The Unending Coil of Bahamut (Ultimate)’s final battle against Primal Bahamut, this song is masterclass in orchestral majestic bliss, and so on and so forth. I have listened to it about 50 times so far, with each time better than the last. It also plays at one other important point in the expansions that I, again, DARE not spoil, by the way.

And there’s so much more I even haven’t gotten into. Side quests, Raid Battles, FATE Battles, Team compositions for Raid dungeons, Parties, etc. AND, lastly, did I mention I’m STILL on the first expansion ( A Realm Reborn )?! I’m just now checking out the other two towns and their overworlds as part of the larger quest. AND I still have SIX more expansions after this to get through! There’s certainly a LOT of content here, which I can appreciate, but there might be TOO MUCH for me to do in such a short time.

If you’re looking for a Xenoblade -type MMORPG with memorable characters and plenty of engaging story beats to keep you interested, this game will scratch that itch, and then some.

My one complaint is the number of expansions and the amount of story/side content is a bit too overbearing and hand-holdy at times. Other than that, I enjoyed my time with FFXIV and the realm of Eorzea, and I can’t wait to come back for another adventure with the Evercold expansion in 2027.

If you liked this review, be sure to check out my review on Legacy of Kain: Ascendance . Thanks for reading, and I’ll see you next time.

items.title: Review: Final Fantasy XIV on Nintendo Switch 2 is the best version of the game
items.content:
I have wanted to get back into Final Fantasy XIV for quite some time. I am a massive fan of everything it offers, from the art direction to the scope of the world and adventures that are held within it. I love the way that it handles narrative within the MMO format, and the massive range of locations to visit. I really, really love the music (I went to a FFXIV symphony and everything), and just generally the very Final Fantasy design of it.

Related reading: To think that I played this for the first time way back on the PlayStation 3. My thoughts back then.

But – and it’s a big but – Final Fantasy XIV is a MMO, and MMOs do demand a time commitment, both in terms of the raw hours you plug into it, and the frequency with which you need to play. Take a big break from an MMO, and it just becomes progressively more difficult to step back into.

I tried to get back into FFXIV once when I first picked up the ROG Xbox Ally . The device handled the game just lovely, but I’m not a frequent PC player, and so at some point I put the device down, took a long break, and just… let my subscription slip again.

I am, however, a frequent Nintendo Switch 2 player. By that I mean “daily”. And so now, with the game’s little icon sitting right there on my Switch 2 home screen, I’ve been logging in for at least a little playtime every day. I’ve already made significantly more progress than I did on the ROG.

Final Fantasy XIV plays just lovely on Switch 2, to start with that important point. The console’s screen is just large enough to be able to handle the very busy interface (it’s an MMO, it’s necessary) without distracting from the core action when you want to watch the fireworks. The game’s visual engine is just now ever-so-slightly showing its age with relatively primitive character models and textures – it has been going for something like 13 years at this point – but the art direction is still as stunning as ever, and I’ve loved revisiting my favourite parts of the world from my first playthrough.

Speaking of, I have started a totally fresh character and save file (I wouldn’t even be able to track down my original avatar from a decade ago, if she still exists on servers somewhere, even if I wanted to. I can’t remember my username, password, or the email address it was attached to). I love how it’s possible to play through all the base game and early expansions with NPCs, and not rely on parties of humans for the various dungeons. If you’ve ever played a FFXIV dungeon before, you’ll know that human allies tend to… well, race through it. One of the few unpleasant memories I have from my first playthrough of Final Fantasy XIV was getting to the very final dungeon of the base game and basically missing the whole thing (and being left behind) because I was trying to follow the story. The conclusion to literally dozens of hours of play.

Now, thanks to NPCs, you can enjoy most of the many expansions and all the stories within them at your own pace. And enjoy the typically excellent music, enemy layouts and dungeon design without feeling rushed, too. I even took time to take screenshots, which is one of my favourite ways to log my adventures in this game.

There is a downside, though. Because Square Enix wants to funnel players into the later expansions where, from their perspective, all the value to the players is, they’ve taken steps to streamline the earlier parts of the game, meaning that you accumulate experience points much (much) faster, and have to do far (far) fewer quests along the way. I have been exclusively undertaking the main quest line, with no side quests, let alone grinding, and my avatar is more than twice the minimum recommended level for any given quest or boss battle.

I understand why they did this, because otherwise it would be a truly intimidating, overwhelming task for a completely new player to get up to the newer expansions, but it means that those same players don’t get to spend enough time in parts of the world to really enjoy their contribution to the whole. The major cities are fine, but you’ll fly through little town areas where previously you’d spend a gaming session or two completing all the side quests. They’re barely blips and blink-and-you’ll-miss-them moments now, which really messes with the pacing for what was previously a truly wonderfully paced game that slowly walked you from one wonder to the next.

I don’t necessarily know what the solution is there, though if it were possible, I would have appreciated the option to toggle whether I wanted the accelerating levelling on or not.

Still, that’s my only gripe. The only other minor issue is that, when it comes to the chat, the Switch’s virtual keyboard doesn’t exactly allow for the same typing speed as a proper keyboard. I don’t even know if it’s possible to connect a Bluetooth keyboard to the Switch 2, as I haven’t tried yet, but even if it were possible, that would significantly undermine the portability of the experience. Currently I haven’t been social enough in FFXIV to require the chat function much, but I can see that becoming an issue later on in the game.

Those are only minor quibbles, obviously, set against a game that is hundreds upon hundreds of hours in scope, and now in an extremely portable and accessible format. FFXIV is a hobby all by itself, and now I can embrace and indulge it in full.

items.content:
Summer is here once more, with fireworks lighting the night sky and festive decorations adorning the streets below. The sandy shores of Costa del Sol offer the perfect respite from the sweltering heat, so it’s time to dive right in and make a splash at the Moonfire Faire!

Event Duration

From Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 9:00 (BST) / 18:00 (AEST) to Wednesday, August 26, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. (PDT) / 14:59 (GMT) / 15:59 (BST) / Thursday, 27 August at 0:59 (AEST)

How to Participate

Begin the quest "Earning Your Water Wings" by speaking to Mayaru Moyaru in Limsa Lominsa, Upper Deck (X:11.5 Y:13.8). * Players must be level 30 and above to start the quest.

Rewards

* Certain items available during previous iterations of the event can be purchased via Moonfire Faire vendors. Visit the special site for more details.

items.title: Gather One, Gather All─Yo-kai Watch Returns to Eorzea!
items.summary: Once more, a horde of Yo-kai descends upon Eorzea! Join in the fun and get your paws on weapons, mounts, a framer's kit, and minions─including Jibanyan and Whisper! This time around, the event features three new indoor furnishings: wibbly-w
items.content:
Once more, a horde of Yo-kai descends upon Eorzea! Join in the fun and get your paws on weapons, mounts, a framer's kit, and minions─including Jibanyan and Whisper! This time around, the event features three new indoor furnishings: wibbly-wobbly Jibanyan, wibbly-wobbly Komasan, and wibbly-wobbly USApyon. * This event is identical to the one previously held, with the addition of three indoor furnishing items. * If you have already completed the quest for this event, it cannot be accepted again. However, you may still earn Yo-kai Medals while equipped with a Yo-kai Watch. * During the event, Yo-kai Watches will be available for purchase from recompense officers in major cities.

Event Duration

From Tuesday, August 4, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 9:00 (BST) / 18:00 (AEST) to Monday, October 5, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. (PDT) / 14:59 (GMT) / 15:59 (BST) / Tuesday, 6 October at 1:59 (AEDT) * Dates and times are subject to change.

How to Participate

Speak with the poor-heeled youth on the Steps of Nald (X:9.2 Y:9.1) in Ul'dah. Upon completion of the quest, you will receive a Yo-kai Watch and Yo-kai Medallium which you can use to obtain Yo-kai Medals. * Players must be level 15 and above to start the quest. * Players must have completed one of the following main scenario quests: "The Gridanian Envoy," "The Lominsan Envoy," or "The Ul’dahn Envoy." Don't miss out on this zany collaboration event!

Rewards

Visit the special site for more details.
